Generated from `mp help` of mailypoppins 0.11.0. Run `mp <command> --help` for the same text in your terminal.

Running `mp` with no command opens the terminal UI. Running `mp <selector>` previews a draft without sending it.

## Global options

These work with every command.

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-s, --signature <SIGNATURE>` | Signature to use (overrides config default) |
| `--no-signature` | Skip signature entirely |
| `-A, --account <ACCOUNT>` | Account to use |

## Sending

### mp send

Send a single approved email, or (with `--invite`) a calendar invitation

```sh
mp send [OPTIONS] [SELECTOR]
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `[SELECTOR]` | Draft selector: mp://&lt;account&gt;/drafts/&lt;id&gt;, drafts/&lt;id&gt; or &lt;id&gt; (omit when using `--invite`) |

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-y, --yes` | Skip confirmation prompt |
| `--invite` | Send an iMIP calendar invitation (METHOD:REQUEST) instead of a draft. Attendees come from `--to`/`--cc`; the subject is used as the event summary. Requires `--to`, `--start` and `--subject`; a timed event also needs one of `--end`/`--duration`, an all-day event (a bare date `--start`) does not |
| `--to <TO>` | Invite recipient(s), comma-separated (invite mode; ATTENDEE + To) |
| `--cc <CC>` | Invite CC recipient(s), comma-separated (invite mode; ATTENDEE + Cc) |
| `--subject <SUBJECT>` | Event subject / summary (invite mode) |
| `--start <START>` | Event start. Local time (2026-07-20T14:00 or "2026-07-20 14:00") or RFC3339 with offset (2026-07-20T14:00:00+02:00, ...Z). A bare date (2026-12-24) makes an all-day event. Invite mode |
| `--end <END>` | Event end, the same kind as `--start`. For an all-day event it is the last day, inclusive (`--start` 2026-12-24 `--end` 2027-01-08 covers 24 Dec through 8 Jan); omit it for a single day. A timed event needs this or `--duration` |
| `--duration <DURATION>` | Event duration instead of `--end`: ISO8601 (PT1H30M) or short (1h30m); whole days (P3D, 3d) for an all-day event |
| `--location <LOCATION>` | Optional event location (invite mode) |
| `--description <DESCRIPTION>` | Optional event description / body (invite mode) |
| `--uid <UID>` | Re-send an invitation already sent, as an update: give its UID (the `UID:` line of its preview or its invite.ics) and a higher `--sequence`. Calendar clients replace the event only when the UID is the same and the SEQUENCE is higher than the one they hold; without `--uid` a fresh UID is minted (a new event) |
| `--sequence <N>` | The update's SEQUENCE, higher than the last one sent for this UID (the first invitation goes out as 0, so a first update is 1). Needs `--uid` |

## Reading and syncing

### mp sync

Sync mailboxes from the server into the local store

```sh

```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-n, --limit <LIMIT>` | Max messages per mailbox. Default: `50`. |
| `--mailbox <MAILBOX>` | Mailboxes to sync (default: INBOX, Archive, Sent) |
| `--dry-run` | Show what would be ingested without writing anything |
| `--all-accounts` | Sync every configured account (failures are named at the end; exit code 1 if any account failed) |

List received messages from the local store (offline)


| --- | --- |
| `--mailbox <MAILBOX>` | Mailbox to list (role, slug or sidebar label). Default: every mailbox of the account, grouped |
| `-n, --limit <LIMIT>` | Max messages per mailbox listed. Default: `20`. |

Print one received message from the local store (offline)


| Option | Description |

| `--json` | Emit one JSON object (headers, attachments and body) instead |

### mp search

Search emails with one grammar that every backend speaks.

```text
Fields (combine freely, implicit AND between them):
  from:  to:  cc:  subject:  body:  filename:   match a field
  has:attachment                                 only mail with an attachment
  before:YYYY-MM-DD  after:YYYY-MM-DD             a date range (since: aliases after:)
  in:MAILBOX                                      scope to one mailbox
  message-id:<id>                                 exact Message-ID lookup

Operators:
  "a phrase"        a quoted phrase is one term
  a OR b            either term
  (a OR b)          a parenthesised OR group, AND-ed with the rest

Examples:
  mp search 'from:boss@corp.com (invoice OR receipt) has:attachment'
  mp search --from boss@corp.com --has-attachment 'invoice OR receipt'
  mp search 'subject:"quarterly report" after:2026-01-01 before:2026-07-01'
  mp search --local 'from:ada ledger'
```

Backend honesty: on Gmail and Exchange every term runs server-side. On plain IMAP has:attachment has no server key, so it is answered from the local store (synced mail only) and the run prints a warning. filename: is Gmail/Exchange/`--local` only.

```sh
mp search [OPTIONS] [QUERY]
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `[QUERY]` | Search query. One grammar for every backend: fields from: to: cc: subject: body: filename:, the flag has:attachment, dates before:YYYY-MM-DD / after:YYYY-MM-DD (since: aliases after:), quoted "phrases", OR and (a OR b) groups, plus in: and message-id:. Combine with the flags below; they build the same query |

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--mailbox <MAILBOX>` | Mailbox to search (default: all the account's mailboxes) |
| `--from <FROM>` | Match the sender (from:) |
| `--to <TO>` | Match a recipient (to:) |
| `--cc <CC>` | Match a Cc recipient (cc:) |
| `--subject <SUBJECT>` | Match the subject (subject:) |
| `--body <BODY>` | Match the body (body:) |
| `--filename <FILENAME>` | Match an attachment filename (Gmail/Exchange/`--local` only) |
| `--has-attachment` | Only mail carrying an attachment (has:attachment) |
| `--after <AFTER>` | On or after this date, YYYY-MM-DD (after:) |
| `--before <BEFORE>` | Strictly before this date, YYYY-MM-DD (before:) |
| `-n, --limit <LIMIT>` | Max results. Default: `20`. |
| `--full` | Show full body instead of preview |
| `--local` | Search the local store's full-text index instead of the server (offline, ranked, covers every synced mailbox at once) |


## Daemon and automation

### mp daemon

Manage the local mailypoppins daemon (run, start, status, stop, restart)

```sh
mp daemon [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

| Subcommand | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`run`](#mp-daemon-run) | Run the daemon in the foreground; never connects to another daemon |
| [`start`](#mp-daemon-start) | Start a detached daemon and return once it answers |
| [`status`](#mp-daemon-status) | Report whether a daemon is running against this data directory |
| [`stop`](#mp-daemon-stop) | Ask the running daemon to shut down |
| [`restart`](#mp-daemon-restart) | Stop the running daemon and start this executable's daemon |
| [`install-service`](#mp-daemon-install-service) | Install the login-start service for this user and enable it |
| [`uninstall-service`](#mp-daemon-uninstall-service) | Disable the login-start service and remove its file |
| [`health`](#mp-daemon-health) | Report the running daemon's health, its counters and its checks |
| [`logs`](#mp-daemon-logs) | Print the tail of the daemon's own structured log |
| [`support-bundle`](#mp-daemon-support-bundle) | Write a redacted support bundle and say what went into it |

#### mp daemon run

Run the daemon in the foreground; never connects to another daemon

```sh
mp daemon run [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--foreground-logs` | Echo lifecycle logs to stderr as well as to the log directory |

#### mp daemon start

Start a detached daemon and return once it answers

```sh
mp daemon start [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--timeout-secs <TIMEOUT_SECS>` | Seconds to wait for the daemon to become ready. Default: `10`. |

#### mp daemon status

Report whether a daemon is running against this data directory

```sh
mp daemon status [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | Print one JSON object instead of a human-readable summary |

#### mp daemon stop

Ask the running daemon to shut down

```sh
mp daemon stop [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--timeout-secs <TIMEOUT_SECS>` | Seconds to wait for the daemon to go away, counted after the grace. Default: `10`. |
| `--grace-secs <GRACE_SECS>` | Seconds the daemon may spend settling work in flight (0 waits none) |

#### mp daemon restart

## Maintenance

### mp store

Local store maintenance (retention garbage collection)

```sh
mp store [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

| Subcommand | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`gc`](#mp-store-gc) | Run the retention sweep now: evict cached blobs over the disk cap |

#### mp store gc

Run the retention sweep now: evict cached blobs over the disk cap.

The first over-cap run only warns and records a marker; run it again to evict. `--dry-run` prints what would go without touching anything. A run that would reclaim more than half the store's blob bytes is refused without `--force` (a fat-finger guard while on-demand re-fetch, #0085, does not yet exist).

```sh
mp store gc [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--dry-run` | Print what would be evicted and stop; change nothing |
| `--force` | Evict even when the plan would reclaim more than half the store |
| `--all-accounts` | Sweep every configured account rather than just the default / `-A` |

### mp cutover

Report what is left of the file-era `.md` tree, and import its drafts.

Assigns an `id:` frontmatter field to any draft that has none, so a file-era draft becomes addressable by selector, then names the file-era mailbox directories nothing reads any more and prints the command that removes them. It deletes nothing itself. `--dry-run` writes not even the `id:` field. Covers every configured account unless `-A` names one.

```sh
mp cutover [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--dry-run` | Report only; write nothing at all |

### mp dump-keys

Dump the TUI key bindings from the single KEYMAP source of truth.

Markdown by default; `--json` emits the section-grouped shape the website consumes. Regenerate the site data with: `mp dump-keys --json > website/src/data/tui-keys.json` (see scripts/regen-website-keys.sh).

```sh
mp dump-keys [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | Emit JSON grouped by section instead of Markdown |

### mp dump-mailbox

Dump message envelopes from the local message store as NDJSON.

Offline: reads the local store only, never the network. One compact JSON object per line, with the fields account, mailbox, message\_id, from, to, cc, subject, date\_sort, flags, attachments (name + size) and invite. No filesystem paths appear in the output.

Records are sorted by account, mailbox, date\_sort, message\_id and subject (the message's uid breaks remaining ties without being emitted), so two runs over an unchanged store are byte-identical.

Dumps every configured account by default; `-A/--account` restricts it to one, `--mailbox` to the named mailboxes.

```sh
mp dump-mailbox [OPTIONS] --json
```

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | Emit newline-delimited JSON. Currently the only output format, and required, so a later default cannot silently change this one |
| `--mailbox <MAILBOX>` | Mailbox to dump (role, slug or sidebar label; repeatable). Default: every mailbox of every selected account |
